title: Navigation reports
summary: Scanning a system's navigation beacon now gives you a navigation report of it - its stations, gates, planets and moons, the hostile and friendly ships about, monsters and resources - instead of lifting the fog, and stations in other systems buy the reports, paying more the further away they are. Landing no longer waits for pictures: a planet's ground and buildings are made from procedural placeholders and take the real pictures in place as they arrive. The health gauge stands on its own with a fuel ring round it, the event log and the loading console are one console with icon tabs, probes can be moved as a group, and shields recharging and the hull mending now burn fuel. Asteroids show again.

steps.title: Landing never waits for pictures
steps.text: A planet's ground, buildings and props were made from the real pictures' pixels, so a surface waited for them before it could show. Now a picture that isn't in yet stands in as a procedural placeholder of exactly its size: the ground and the buildings are made from it at once and made again in place, on a worker, when the real picture arrives. Walls, floors and roofs show a simple stub and are composed on worker threads - they had cost up to 21 ms each in the frame.

steps.title: The gauge on its own, fuel round it
steps.text: The health gauge stands on its own: no panel, no numbers or labels (hover the rings for them), no drachmas (they show at stations and in the inventory). In space a third ring of amber liquid round the shield ring shows your fuel; its rim turns red when there isn't enough left for a jump.

steps.title: One console, two tabs
steps.text: The event log and the loading console are one console now: two icon tabs at its top switch between them. The loading tab keeps its history, the memory pool, the progress bar and the memory map, and keeps recording while hidden; a thin line under its icon shows the progress from either tab. Its text follows the HUD's text size, like the log's.

steps.title: Navigation reports
steps.text: Scanning a system's navigation beacon no longer lifts its fog: it gives you a navigation report of the system as it is - its stations and who holds them, its jump gates, its planets and moons (the landable ones in green), the ships about (hostile ones by who they are, friendly and neutral ones by empire, all by trade), monsters, asteroids, wrecks and signals - shown at once.

steps.title: Selling reports
steps.text: Stations in other systems buy navigation reports: 60 drachmas, plus 70 for every jump between the two systems and 10 for each of the report's system's stations - worthless in its own system. A beacon gives one copy a visit: leave the system and come back for another.

steps.text: On the system map's probe scanner, a gold handle above the probes moves them all at once, keeping their formation (so does Shift + drag on any probe); the wheel over the handle spreads them out or draws them in round their middle, and Shift + wheel over a probe changes every probe's reach.

steps.title: Recharging burns fuel
steps.text: Your ship's shields recharging and its hull mending itself burn fuel as they come back: 0.02 a shield point (a full 100: 2 fuel) and 0.05 a hull point (100: 5) - a jump is 10. With a little fuel you get back what it pays for; out of fuel, neither recharges.

steps.title: Fixes
steps.text: Asteroids show again (a rock spawned off screen stopped its own fade-in, so every rock of a streamed system stayed invisible). The loading tab's text was drawn at a fixed small size. A Minoan axe guard chasing a foe that had just died errored every frame.

review.intro: Patch 0015 in code: navigation reports (nav_reports.gd, nav_report_panel.gd; galaxy.gd keeps them and no longer lifts the fog; main.gd's beacon scan; items.gd / player_data.gd for the report item; station_menu.gd sells them by distance); placeholders for planets' ground and buildings (proc_art.gd image_now, terrain_tiles.gd and minoan_tiles.gd made from placeholder images and made again in place, walls and floors composed on workers; planet_surface.gd waits for nothing); the gauge on its own with a fuel ring (health_gauge.gd, hud.gd); one console with tabs (event_log.gd); probes moved as a group (pages/map_page.gd); shields and hull burning fuel (ship.gd, shipyard.gd); and fixes (main.gd's fade-in, surface_props.gd). Tests: test_fog's report, test_play's streaming fade, test_mining_industry's group moves, test_damage_feedback's fuel.

+## shown at once (NavReportPanel) and put in your hold as an item,
+## "navrep:<system id>". Stations in OTHER systems buy reports: the further
+## (jumps between the systems) the more they pay; worthless in its own system.
+## One report a visit: a beacon gives another only after you've left the system
+## and come back (Galaxy.jumps). Reports are kept with the galaxy (Galaxy.reports).
+
+const PREFIX := "navrep:"
+## A report's price: BASE + PER_JUMP a jump away (+ PER_STATION for each of its
+## system's stations: busier systems' charts sell better).
+const BASE := 60
+const PER_JUMP := 70
+const PER_STATION := 10
+
+
+static func id_for(sys_id: String) -> String:
+	return PREFIX + sys_id
+
+
+static func is_report(id: String) -> bool:
+	return id.begins_with(PREFIX)
+
+
+static func system_of(id: String) -> String:
+	return id.substr(PREFIX.length()) if is_report(id) else ""
+
+
+static func valid(id: String) -> bool:
+	return is_report(id) and Galaxy.SYSTEMS.has(system_of(id))
+
+
+## The item: kind "report" (sold at stations, never in "sell all cargo").
+static func info(id: String) -> Dictionary:
+	if not valid(id):
+		return {}
+	var sys := system_of(id)
+	var r: Dictionary = Galaxy.reports.get(sys, {})
+	var desc := "A navigation report of the %s system, made at its beacon. Stations in other systems buy it - the further from %s, the more they pay; worthless in its own system." % [name_of(sys), name_of(sys)]
+	if not r.is_empty():
+		desc += "\n%s" % summary(r)
+	return {"name": "Nav Report: %s" % name_of(sys), "kind": "report", "value": 0, "desc": desc}
+
+
+static func name_of(sys: String) -> String:
+	return str(Galaxy.SYSTEMS.get(sys, {}).get("name", sys))
+
+
+## Jumps between two systems (the shortest way along the lanes); -1 if none.
+static func jumps(a: String, b: String) -> int:
+	if a == b:
+		return 0
+	var seen := {a: 0}
+	var q: Array = [a]
+	while not q.is_empty():
+		var s: String = q.pop_front()
+		for n in Galaxy.neighbors(s):
+			if not seen.has(n):
+				seen[n] = seen[s] + 1
+				if n == b:
+					return seen[n]
+				q.append(n)
+	return -1
+
+
+## What a station in system `at` pays for the report of system `sys` (0 there).
+static func price(sys: String, at: String) -> int:
+	var j := jumps(sys, at)
+	if j <= 0:
+		return 0
+	var st: int = Galaxy.system(sys).get("stations", []).size() if Galaxy.systems.has(sys) else 0
+	return BASE + PER_JUMP * j + PER_STATION * st
+
+
+## The report of the system you're in, made from what's in it now (Main's scene).
+static func make(tree: SceneTree, sys: String) -> Dictionary:
+	var r := {"sys": sys, "name": name_of(sys), "owner": Galaxy.empire_name(Galaxy.owner_of(sys)),
+		"stations": [], "bodies": [], "gates": [], "hostile": {}, "friendly": {}, "roles": {},
+		"monsters": [], "rocks": 0, "wrecks": 0, "signals": 0, "made": Time.get_datetime_string_from_system(false, true)}
+	for st in tree.get_nodes_in_group("stations"):
+		r["stations"].append([str(st.get("station_name")), Galaxy.empire_name(str(st.get("empire")))])
+	for b in tree.get_nodes_in_group("planet_bodies"):
+		if str(b.get("title")) == "":
+			continue
+		var parent = b.get("parent_body")
+		var spec = b.get("spec")
+		r["bodies"].append([str(b.title), str(spec.get("name", "")) if spec is Dictionary else "", bool(b.get("landable")),
+			str(parent.title) if parent != null and is_instance_valid(parent) else ""])
+	for g in tree.get_nodes_in_group("gates"):
+		r["gates"].append(str(g.get("target_name")) if str(g.get("target_name")) != "" else name_of(str(g.get("target"))))
+	var main := tree.current_scene
+	for holder in ["enemies", "neutrals"]:
+		var box = main.get(holder) if main else null
+		if box == null:
+			continue
+		for s in (box as Node).get_children():
+			if s.has_method("is_alive") and not s.is_alive():
+				continue
+			if s.get("role") == null:
+				continue
+			if EnemyTypes.MONSTERS.has(str(s.type_id)):   # (a monster)
+				r["monsters"].append(str(s.display_name) if str(s.display_name) != "" else str(EnemyTypes.MONSTERS[s.type_id].get("name", s.type_id)))
+				continue
+			var who: String = Galaxy.empire_name(str(s.empire)) if str(s.empire) != "" else ("Pirates" if str(s.role) == "pirate" else "Independent")
+			var side: String = "hostile" if s.has_method("is_hostile_to_player") and s.is_hostile_to_player() else "friendly"
+			r[side][who] = int(r[side].get(who, 0)) + 1
+			var role: String = str(s.role) if str(s.role) != "" else "other"
+			r["roles"][role] = int(r["roles"].get(role, 0)) + 1
+	r["rocks"] = tree.get_nodes_in_group("asteroids").size()
+	r["wrecks"] = tree.get_nodes_in_group("wrecks").filter(func(w): return not w.get("salvaged")).size()
+	r["signals"] = tree.get_nodes_in_group("signal_beacons").size()
+	return r
+
+
+static func total(d: Dictionary) -> int:
+	var n := 0
+	for k in d:
+		n += int(d[k])
+	return n
+
+
+## "3 stations, 7 planets and moons, 2 gates; 4 hostile ships, 12 others; 40 asteroids".
+static func summary(r: Dictionary) -> String:
+	return "%d stations, %d planets and moons, %d gates; %d hostile ships, %d others%s; %d asteroids" % [
+		r["stations"].size(), r["bodies"].size(), r["gates"].size(), total(r["hostile"]), total(r["friendly"]),
+		(", %d monsters" % r["monsters"].size()) if not r["monsters"].is_empty() else "", int(r["rocks"])]
+
+
+## The item's icon: a chart slate - an orbit, a star, a course across it.
+static func draw_icon(ci: CanvasItem, _id: String, rect: Rect2, dim := false) -> void:

+	ci.draw_circle(c + Vector2(0, s * 0.05), s * 0.16, Color(1.0, 0.82, 0.4, a))
+	ci.draw_circle(c + Vector2(s * 0.5, s * 0.05), s * 0.09, Color(0.5, 0.75, 1.0, a))
+	ci.draw_line(c + Vector2(-s * 0.6, s * 0.7), c + Vector2(s * 0.6, -s * 0.65), Color(1.0, 0.7, 0.3, 0.9 * a), maxf(1.0, s * 0.07), true)
